page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro system and powered by AWS Graviton ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processors. Operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz, the instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading contention. The platform allocates 64 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. In addition to 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and zero GPU accelerators, the instance bundles a 950 GB local NVMe solid-state drive for high-speed ephemeral storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent compute throughput paired with notable memory write efficiency. In uncached large-block write tests, memory bandwidth reached 100.5 GB/sec, ranking in the top quartile alongside a strong PassMark memory score of 2913.56. General computational throughput tests, including stress-ng multi-core (24495.36) and Geekbench multi-core (12993.0), demonstrate standard mid-range results. In contrast, the system yielded lower-quartile outcomes in PassMark CPU encryption tests (2224.38) and 7B model prompt processing throughput (28.22 tokens/sec).

From an operational standpoint, the combination of dedicated ARM64 cores and direct-attached NVMe storage provides high density and predictable execution without local disk access fees. Workloads dependent on legacy x86 instruction sets or hardware-accelerated encryption may encounter architectural constraints. The hardware profile is best suited for distributed databases, caching clusters requiring rapid local persistence, software compilation pipelines, and containerized web application backends.
description: Amazon Web Services m7gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM-based cloud instance powered by 16 physical cores of the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz without multithreading. It features 64 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, alongside 8 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and no hardware GPU accelerators. A key component of this server is the included 950 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling high-speed scratch and cache operations. Benchmark data reveals strong uncached memory write throughput exceeding 100 GB/sec and upper-quartile PassMark memory results, balanced by mid-tier multi-core computing metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench. Cryptographic and prompt-processing workloads demonstrate lower comparative efficiency. Given its dedicated ARM core configuration and local solid-state capacity, the m7gd.4xlarge functions effectively for web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed databases requiring low-latency scratch storage.
